mechanisms.summary: Rational factor-coded singular Gaussian prior, positive noise floor, innovation inverse and Joseph posterior identity.
boundaries: Exact rational factors, positive floor, singular/zero priors and rectangular observation operators are supported within declared dimension/bit caps.
The posterior gain is solved on observation space without inverting the prior; Joseph parameters are computed exactly.
Independent Gaussian law interpretation and source disintegration theorem remain separate from a new Lean/kernel or host-refinement proof.

mechanisms.section: §4 Proposition 4.1 equations (14)-(18); §5 Lemma 5.1 and Theorem 5.2 equations (19)-(22)
mechanisms.summary: Candidate Joseph covariance, excess-covariance residual identity and inverse-free score E(F)*(sigma+||d||²)/sigma².
boundaries: Exact candidate Joseph parameters, full residual energy, score and cross-multiplied sufficient tolerance are recomputed from supplied model and gain.
The score bounds squared W2 under the source's declared independent Gaussian interpretation; it is not the optimal Wasserstein distance.
Finite tests and exact checks do not replay the source's measure-level/formal proof or prove unrestricted statistical validity.

mechanisms.summary: Complete self-adjoint orthogonal input/output packets and two-sided residual decomposition.
boundaries: gaussian_packet_energy checks exact symmetry, idempotence, orthogonality and completeness of both families and computes every two-sided residual energy.
Generic PacketSystem requires hilbert_certificate for self-adjointness; its basic certificate allows oblique packets.
Partial, oblique or overlapping families cannot establish complete residual stopping evidence.
Fixed finite packet-energy machinery does not implement the source's selected cache/trajectory or majorant proposal batch.

mechanisms.section: §9 Definition 9.1 and Proposition 9.2 equations (33)-(36); §10 Proposition 10.1, Lemma 10.2 equations (37)-(39)
mechanisms.summary: Exact maximum-energy packet cache with invariant Ga=QaF(B), identical greedy trajectory and rational finite fuel.
boundaries: No exact Gaussian selective cache, prepared kernel, strict tie-selection or rational fuel API was found.
Both model operators and fixed complete output packets must be declared; selection completeness is not inferred from sampled labels.
A resource-capped host execution may fail even though the source's ideal finite-success theorem applies.

mechanisms.section: §11 equation (40), precisionFor equation (41), Theorem 11.1; §12 equation (42), Theorem 12.1
mechanisms.summary: Formal operation-by-operation dyadic graph, coefficient budgets, automatic fallback and declared result-array equality.
boundaries: The new direct dyadic finite evaluator is a separate implementation; the formal graph, scoreRoundCoeff, precisionFor fallback and formal evaluator/result equality have not been ported.
Direct final-value enclosures do not reproduce operation-by-operation rounded outputs from the paper.
Law tolerance epsilon and output radius delta retain distinct meanings; neither certifies a Gaussian from center-only covariance.

mechanisms.section: §15 rounded-cache counterexample and rounded full-gain branch; §§16-17.3
mechanisms.summary: Rounded full-gain perturbation contract and limits of exact cache/sequential reuse.
boundaries: Independent rounding of gain and residual centers destroys the exact-cache invariant; the source gives a scalar counterexample.
Rounded selective caches, sequential filtering, changing hierarchies, executable sampling and universal parser/host refinement are separate extensions.
Archived formal build and bounded producer tests are distinct evidence; no fresh Lean build or universal host refinement is asserted here.

mechanisms.section: §1 reading contract; §2 finite Gaussian state/observation model
mechanisms.summary: Existing discrete finite Bayesian update/filter APIs are adjacent machinery.
boundaries: These APIs use finite probability vectors and floating likelihood arithmetic.
They do not implement the source's rational Gaussian gain, Joseph covariance, packet cache, Wasserstein certificate or dyadic parameter output.

mechanisms.section: Definitions 2.1 and 3.1; Theorems 3.2 and 3.4; §5 Proposition 5.1; §14 Theorem 14.1
mechanisms.summary: Raw admissible routes, endpoint grouping, concrete route-state retention and conditional finite-depth exploration.
boundaries: Existing finite typed quiver paths and declared matrix realizations provide a restricted homogeneous linear sector.
No general state-dependent admissible grammar explorer retaining actual per-route endpoints, explicit truncation records and finite one-step family-check scope was found.
A canonical endpoint key does not justify representative substitution for future continuations.
Depth-dependent state, immutable callback semantics and complete exposed fibers are separate assumptions.

mechanisms.summary: Labeled partial action descends exactly when equivalent representatives have identical enabled labels and equivalent successors.
boundaries: No generic finite continuation-domain/successor compatibility checker was found.
Existing declared linear relation certificates are not a checker for nonlinear state-dependent quotient descent.
Graph-isomorphism keys can merge two P3 representatives whose attach-at-vertex-0 successors are nonisomorphic; both domain and successor clauses must be checked.
Transported direction identifiers require additional coherence data.

mechanisms.summary: Ordered multi-input tree syntax, exact Catalan counts and finite evaluation.
boundaries: Existing ordered trees have one implicit operation per arity and an unlabeled leaf, not the paper's general typed symbol/seed signature with partial admissibility.
Finite enumeration uses explicit combinatorial caps; the entire recursively generated free syntax space is not returned.
Exact evaluation depends on exact supplied multilinear operations; general associativity or commutativity is not inferred from finite agreement.

mechanisms.section: Definition 7.1, Theorem 7.2, Example 7.4; §8 finite family and recurrence checker boundary
mechanisms.summary: All-parameter semiconjugacy and relation preservation versus exact finite prefix recurrence fitting.
boundaries: Exact inclusive partial sums and prefix-supported recurrence fitting are available.
No general all-parameter family-semiconjugacy API or finite raw-state family checker from this companion was found.
A fitted finite prefix does not prove an unseen all-index recurrence.
The existing finite_difference is forward difference and should not be identified with the paper's backward D(a)_n=a_n-a_(n-1) without a boundary/index translation.

mechanisms.section: Definition 9.1, Theorem 9.3 equation (3), Example 9.2, §9.1; Theorem 11.1 equation (5)
mechanisms.summary: Cross-fiber paired admissible covers and product-sum affine endpoint/model-error envelopes.
boundaries: No dedicated exact interval-direction grid/cover or variable-step affine recurrence envelope API was found.
A finite net of the sampled-state fiber does not automatically cover the exact-state fiber.
Transported controls can increase the state sensitivity from L to L+M.
An endpoint error bound alone does not establish convergence, quotient-key equality or symbolic identity.

mechanisms.summary: Summable-step Cauchy completion and dyadic infinite tails.
boundaries: A finite suffix sum or batch diameter cannot certify the omitted infinite tail.
Limit existence requires a complete target; preservation of validity requires a closed validity region or another argument.
Dyadic tail 2^-N and periodic branch limit 5/7 follow from the source's geometric-series theorem; finite prefixes alone are not proofs.
No general metric completion API was found.

mechanisms.summary: Finite fixed-depth prefix cylinder partitions and transfer through complete intermediate resolutions.
boundaries: Finite coordinate masks can be represented as exact packet projectors and finite transfer products.
No dedicated route-cylinder builder verifies fixed ambient depth, prefix freedom and route coverage.
Countable sums are strong limits with stated directed/rectangular summation; they are not finite API claims or arbitrary norm-convergent rearrangements.
A cut meeting all infinite routes need not cover the supplied finite depth.

mechanisms.section: §15.4 prime congruence lifts; §16.4 declared discrete metric choices
mechanisms.summary: Finite prime polynomial correction fibers and explicit compatible residue branches.
boundaries: The prime-field correction solver verifies supplied finite polynomial systems; a composite base does not satisfy the derivative/unit implication.
Finite towers and stable cores cover only declared levels, not p-adic limit existence or topology.
FiniteLiftForest is an explicit inverse system, not the paper's general state-dependent route explorer.
The paper's discrete finite model must not be confused with a p-adic inverse-limit metric.

mechanisms.summary: Infinite weighted route-count criteria and fair countable or priority scheduling.
boundaries: A prefix entropy maximum or finite growth polynomial does not determine infinite limsup entropy or a convergence radius.
A branching upper bound and positive step-cost lower bound supply a sufficient criterion; their converse need not hold for a general grammar.
Fair countable dovetailing and complete general route-cost accounting are not implemented by the existing finite graph/lift structures.
Formal companion covers selected natural-number envelopes and masks, not full real metric completion or arbitrary typed partial syntax.

mechanisms.summary: Positive-sign normalized synthesis and coherent-state Fourier transport.
boundaries: Numerical cyclic character projectors are related machinery; no dedicated exact positive-sign normalized Fourier constructor was located.
Source synthesis F[n,a]=N^-1/2 exp(2*pi*i*n*a/N); cyclic labels depend on the supplied symmetry convention.

mechanisms.summary: Integer Ramanujan signal from coprime residue support and Fourier energy.
boundaries: Scalar Möbius infrastructure exists, but no dedicated Ramanujan signal/support/energy API was located.
The q=1 branch includes the coprime label 0.

mechanisms.summary: Exact rational character-order shell projector and unions of divisor classes.
boundaries: Generic rational spectral packets construct cyclic-shift shells using cyclotomic characteristic factors.
Dedicated order labeling and Ramanujan-kernel formula are absent; generic tests do not specifically validate the divisor-shell formula.
Kernel normalization is 1/N, including d<N.

mechanisms.summary: Selector, complementary residual and complete orthogonal reconstruction.
boundaries: A proper selector discards the complement; invertible basis transport is different from projection.
Orthogonal energy geometry requires self-adjointness beyond the basic algebraic packet certificate.

mechanisms.summary: Coefficient/sample residue lanes and formal root-rotation masks.
boundaries: Finite coefficient/sample lanes exist.
No generic infinite formal-series root-rotation projector was located; source formal identity needs roots of unity and 1/L, without analytic convergence.

mechanisms.summary: Interleaving, Fourier twiddles and offset-dependent alias reconstruction.
boundaries: Interleaving exists; dedicated source Fourier-twiddle and decimation-alias equations/tests were not located.
Source assumes N=L*M. One sample lane loses alias separation; sample-residue masks are different from character-order shells.

mechanisms.summary: Literal arithmetic/projector/unitary chain and transformed outcome probabilities.
boundaries: Generic components can express the example, but its literal c,b,x,F,D,P,u,psi,chi source fixture and exact probabilities 1/0 were not located.
No efficient gate decomposition, quantum speedup or advantage follows from finite equalities.

mechanisms.summary: Projective effects, outcome probabilities and conditional Lüders branches.
boundaries: Nonselective packet dephasing and finite Kraus action exist.
Dedicated conditional Lüders normalization/probabilities were not located; normalize only nonzero branches.
Effects alone do not specify the measurement instrument.

mechanisms.summary: Exact Q^4 multiplication/conjugation for a+b*sqrt(3)+i*(c+d*sqrt(3)).
boundaries: No dedicated tuple arithmetic/sound complex-interpretation API or test was found.
General SymPy exact expressions are related infrastructure, not a reproduction of the source's finite formal certificate.

mechanisms.summary: Constant initial histogram and selected probability sin²(theta/2).
boundaries: Generic finite circuit interference exists; no dedicated chi_theta=v_plus+exp(i*theta)*v_minus API/test was located.
Continuous parameter variation remains finite dimensional and does not imply an infinite operator theorem.

mechanisms.summary: Nonselective density-matrix dephasing of the source example.
boundaries: Generic dephasing exists; source-specific selected probability 1/3 is not covered by the located tests.
Coherent absolute-amplitude replacement differs from density-matrix dephasing.
QA20 lies outside the source's inherited finite quantum Lean package.

mechanisms.summary: Coordinate Clifford actions and finite Dirac mass-shell symbol.
boundaries: Literal coordinate entries are NumPy complex arrays; general symbol evaluation is numerical.
Spinor coordinate order and alpha_y*e0=i*e3 match the traditional source.
No unbounded Dirac domain or continuum Hilbert operator is constructed.

mechanisms.summary: Centered Fourier multiplier p=2*pi*n, sin(h*p)/h, filled at zero mesh.
boundaries: Finite mode labels, signed/zero/tiny mesh and finite-range arithmetic are tested.
Dedicated generator/dispersion quadratic-error bound with C(n)=sqrt(sum|p_j|^6)/6 is not implemented.
This is a continuum-torus multiplier; no sampled-grid Hilbert norm, Nyquist restriction or label recovery is implied.

mechanisms.summary: Closed trigonometric propagator including zero-energy identity.
boundaries: Numerical finite matrices support real signed time/mass and independent eigensystem/group-law controls.
Dedicated positive/negative spectral-projector API P_plusminus=(I+-H/E)/2 was not located.
General-symbol splitting is traditional prose, beyond matching checked Block44 claims.

mechanisms.summary: Normalized torus finite packet assembly and norm conservation.
boundaries: Per-mode evolution and generic finite packets exist, but no dedicated torus Fourier isometry, three-mode source fixture or packet-conservation test was located.
Parseval uses the source's normalized torus Fourier convention.
Infinite support and cutoff removal are separate claims.

mechanisms.summary: Fixed-mode and finite-packet quadratic propagator consistency.
boundaries: Generic finite exponential comparisons are available, not a source-specific quadratic convergence envelope.
Mode, support, amplitudes and time are fixed; constants grow with momentum.

mechanisms.summary: Algebraic max-norm to Hilbert Euclidean-norm generator/exponential bridge.
boundaries: General exact coordinate maps are related infrastructure; no dedicated normed bridge or matching test was located.
The identity coordinate map between these norms is not an isometry.
The full PH09 conclusion is traditional prose beyond the checked coordinate ingredients.

mechanisms.section: §11, finite Hermitian Duhamel lemma and PH11
mechanisms.summary: All-real-time Hermitian |t| operator bound and weighted finite-packet envelope.
boundaries: Existing bound is a general exponential estimate with nonnegative-time API, not the sharp ||exp(-itA)-exp(-itB)||<=|t|*||A-B|| source contract.
Amplitude-weighted packet bound is absent.
PH11 is explicitly beyond the traditional paper's Block44 checked frontier.

mechanisms.summary: Conservation and comparison of a finite packet's Hamiltonian expectation.
boundaries: Supplied finite symbols/propagators allow direct calculation, but no dedicated conservation/comparison API/test was found.
Squared norm, rest mass, shell energy and Hamiltonian expectation are distinct.
Only each system's own time-independent Hamiltonian is covered; interactions, forcing and time-dependent generators are separate.

mechanisms.section: §5 Theorem 5.2; §12 equation (42) parameter meaning; distinct direct evaluator inspired by §§11-12
mechanisms.summary: Exact rational score/parameters followed by direct outward dyadic floor/ceiling intervals and upper-score/radius verification.
boundaries: This recomputes exact final rational values then encloses endpoints; it is not Core1.0.0's operation-by-operation dyadic graph or its coefficient/fallback proof.
Verification accepts only when the upper squared score passes exact Fraction comparison; a coarse overlapping interval cannot pass.
Mean/covariance radii describe the returned Joseph law, not coordinate error against the exact posterior, and centers are not a separately certified PSD Gaussian.
Caps apply to input and derived rational bits, dimensions, packet count and precision; conservative dyadic pre-scaling can reject values whose reduced endpoint would fit.

validation.scope: Source extraction and API/test mapping; existing related finite tests replayed without asserting universal source theorem verification.

validation.version_boundary: Existing dirac_modes.md cites the 6 October Physics set. This fragment pins the distinct 8 October traditional edition, Block44. Later Block49 Lean artifacts are not evaluated or counted as Python APIs.
non_claims: Related APIs and source-constructible specializations are not counted as complete dedicated implementations.
No finite test establishes unrestricted discovery, unknown-operator coverage, universal statistical validity or continuum convergence.
